subject: making a function to convert ggplot object into shiny app

messages.author: 26b647b408a2e02e
messages.subject: making a function to convert ggplot object into shiny app
parts:
I made a function to convert any ggplot object into a shiny app, because I often want to zoom in the plot for details, and I didn't find simple solution to add interactive zoom.

The function works but I have to specify a conversion function when the axis is in date/date-time because ggplot have a type check for axis and will not convert silently. I can understand the reasoning but that make the "one line conversion" goal difficult.

I think it's unfair to ask Shiny to know the type of axis in brush event, then maybe the only approach left is to inspect ggplot object and guess the type conversion needed. But that seemed quite complex for a simple goal.

I'm wondering if there is a better solution. Any comment?

messages.author: 26b647b408a2e02e
messages.subject: Re: making a function to convert ggplot object into shiny app
parts:
Thanks for the tip. "summarise_layout" do make the inspection a little bit easier. Now it will work with date, datetime automatically.
Though I'm not sure if this method will be stable enough for all kind of cases.

  gb <- ggplot_build(g)
  plot_summary <- summarise_layout(gb)
  x_scale <- plot_summary$xscale[1][[1]]$scale_name
  y_scale <- plot_summary$yscale[1][[1]]$scale_name
  get_trans_fun <- function(axis_scale) {
    switch(axis_scale,
      date = as_date,
      datetime = as_datetime,
      identity)
  }
  x_as <- get_trans_fun(x_scale)
  y_as <- get_trans_fun(y_scale)

messages.subject: Re: making a function to convert ggplot object into shiny app
parts:
Yes I will test against the major version changes. This is also the reason I hesitated to use this method since it rely on not structures that without guarantee to be stable. 

So ggplot is starting to have an API for better interaction with other program/libraries. Ideally if we can add a feature in ggplot API of "summarise_layout" to report the axis types, then it will hide all possible future changes. Previously I thought it's unfair to ask Shiny to know the plot axis type, or ask ggplot to deal with Shiny events. But it should be reasonable to expose some information in API.

I'll submit a feature request in ggplot about this.
